- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "review-blocked follow-up and existing-PR pushes use one-shot Git credentials; the poller does not write `GH_TOKEN` into shared worktree Git configuration" and the broader PR DESCRIPTION commitment that isolation and parity are applied to every relevant surface, including the root `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` that the CI test `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` actually loads.
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` (the root hook, sibling of the already-updated `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` and the just-edited `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`).
  Evidence of absence: The symbol diff summary lists only `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` (lines 348-354 and 642-649) for the merge-guard file; `pr_changed_files.txt` enumerates the same template path but does NOT list `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`. The LAST RUN DIFF touches only the template copy and adds comments around an already-present `re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\+?=", …)`; the root hook is never modified, so commands of the form `COUNT+=1 git push origin feature` (and any other `NAME+=value` prefix before `git`) still slip past the guard's leading-assignment scan that strips `NAME=` prefixes. CI proves the gap: the `lint` job in the failed check-runs context reports `CI jobs that did not succeed: tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` and the job's log ends with `5 failed, 172 passed in 6.64s` from `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` — the exact suite that exercises the root guard's push parsing. Cross-pollination has four reviewers (deepseek, gemini, gpt-6-luna, glm) flagging the same root-vs-template gap; the prior editor summary 5981874432 already noted "The untracked root merge guard is byte-identical to its template" and the last run was the moment to commit that parity into the tracked root, which it did not do.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  PROBLEM: The template recognizes Bash append-assignment prefixes, but the source hook does not. The source hook also remains different from the template, contrary to the byte-for-byte parity assertion in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` line 1000.
  WHY: For a command such as `COUNT+=1 git push origin feature`, the source hook does not consume `COUNT+=1` as an assignment, so it does not recognize the following `git push` and skips the merged-PR check. The supplied CI run confirms the regression: the hook test job failed with 5 failures, causing `lint` to fail.
